text: On Tuesday, Peverell Semiconductors confirmed it had laid off 1,200 staff, the steepest cut in its 43-year history and a stark reminder of how quickly the district’s chip economy has cooled. The Northfold manufacturer, once celebrated for its glass-fronted campus on Bracken Quay, said the reductions were spread across engineering, packaging and support teams after a months-long slowdown in orders from consumer-device makers. Chief executive Mara Elling said the company would “recalibrate for a smaller market” while preserving core research lines on low-power sensors. Local officials, still mindful of the plant’s role in Northfold’s postwar industrial revival, described the news as painful but not unexpected after a year of falling margins and postponed expansion plans.
